prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map supports a layered scene layout: the road and curb are nearest below the camera, the palm trees and streetlights occupy intermediate distances, and the horizon, fence, and sky are farthest; the bright foreground also makes the road-to-curb boundary clearer than in RGB. Across the five frames, the nearest large palm shifts from left-of-centre to partly above and behind the viewpoint before disappearing, consistent with the camera wearer passing it, while the cyclists on the right side of the road become larger and nearer, from roughly 20–30 m away initially to about 5–10 m in the last frame; the cyclists remain roughly 2–5 m from one another. They are to the camera wearer’s right and ahead or alongside, with bicycles below their bodies; nothing visible is within the camera wearer’s arm’s reach, although each bicycle is within its rider’s reach. Absolute metre estimates are unreliable because this is monocular depth, the sky is incorrectly rendered as uniformly far/black, thin structures and people have weak or inconsistent depth, and occlusion ordering among the cyclists is not clearly resolved.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates only a few moving instances against black: people and bicycles are detected on the right side in the later frames, with one small person detection near the centre-right of the second frame and overlapping person/bicycle or motorcycle labels in the third through fifth frames. In context, these instances progress from small and distant to larger and nearer as the camera wearer approaches or passes them, remaining right of the camera and near one another—approximately 2–5 m apart—with bodies above their bicycles; none is within the camera wearer’s arm’s reach. The masks help distinguish overlapping riders and cycles that are small and low-contrast in RGB, but they do not provide metric depth, facing direction, gaze, or reliable front-versus-behind ordering without RGB and size cues. The map is unreliable spatially because masks are tiny or fragmented, labels overlap, a bicycle is sometimes labelled motorcycle, most of the road and fixed scene are omitted, and people or cycles may be partly occluded by one another or clipped at the right edge in the final frame.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is entirely black across all five frames, so it supplies no usable body or hand skeletons and therefore cannot establish body orientation, gaze direction, limb positions, interpersonal facing, or reach. From the RGB alone, the visible people stay on the camera wearer’s right and generally appear side-on or oriented along the road rather than clearly looking toward the camera, but the absent pose detections cannot confirm this. It also cannot separate overlapping bodies, show which person is in front, or reveal any body parts hidden by bicycles, other riders, distance, or the right image boundary. Its failure is likely associated with the people being small, partially occluded, and low-detail, making this map unreliable for spatial analysis in every frame.
